2026-10-20.overview: It's NBA opening week, with three games today and eight more tomorrow, plus two days of Champions League soccer and a handful of weeknight college football games. The outcomes I feel best about are the lopsided or close matchups where a big blowout is unlikely: Barcelona not running away from PSG, Liverpool and Betis not winning by three, Bayern not winning by two against Arsenal, and the full-strength Raptors beating a Bulls team missing its starting center. The best prices look like the Roma and Manchester City games, where the home favorites are missing key players and are priced to win big anyway, and South Alabama at Marshall, where Marshall still doesn't know who its quarterback is. I'm staying off all NBA player bets today and keeping college football to one pick, since both have burned us before.

picks.reason: Toronto is fully healthy at home and favored by about ten, while the Bulls' starting center Nic Claxton is out for two more weeks with a hamstring injury (Basketnews, Fox Sports).

picks.reason: Betis just gave up five at home to Barcelona and are missing striker Cucho Hernandez and Junior Firpo (Sports Mole), while Feyenoord have won five straight. Betis by three is a stretch.

picks.label: Fenerbahce not to win by 3+
picks.reason: Fenerbahce have been outscored badly in Europe this year and Asensio is doubtful, while Slavia lead their league on a four-game winning run. Previews expect a one-goal game.

picks.reason: Bayern are without Olise, who is suspended, and Musiala, who is hurt (Bavarian Football Works), and the books have the game nearly even. A two-goal Bayern win is the unlikely part.

picks.reason: Roma are missing their starting goalkeeper Svilar plus Kone, Cristante and likely Dybala (Yahoo Sports, Sports Mole), and still haven't won in Europe this season. Winning by three with a patched-up side is a big ask.

picks.reason: Haaland has a knock and is expected to be rested, and Semenyo is out for two months (Sports Mole, beIN). City are in poor form and a three-goal margin without their striker is less likely than the price says.

picks.label: South Alabama to win
picks.reason: Marshall's coach won't name a quarterback before kickoff after calling his starter's play horrible (Herald-Dispatch), while South Alabama is unbeaten in conference with a confirmed starter and a strong run game. ESPN's model and the books both side with South Alabama.

Bagent has not thrown a single touchdown pass in his six games this year and Chicago leaned on the run game to win last week, so two touchdown passes from him would be a surprise.

favorites.reason: Tyler Goodson is Dallas's third running back behind Javonte Williams and has averaged only a handful of rushing yards a game over his last thirteen (slate data). Even if Dallas runs out the clock late, he rarely gets enough carries to reach twenty yards.

ESPN's model, our own ratings and Covers' projected score all have Texas winning by double digits.

favorites.reason: Kyler Murray has averaged less than one touchdown pass a game in his eight games for Minnesota (slate data), and Justin Jefferson is still day-to-day with his ankle with Jordan Addison also questionable, per Newsweek and the Vikings' own report. picks.label: Raptors to win
picks.reason: Toronto is fully healthy at home and favored by about ten, while the Bulls' starting center Nic Claxton is out for two more weeks with a hamstring injury (Basketnews, Fox Sports).

picks.label: Barcelona not to win by 2+
picks.reason: The books have this one nearly even, and Barcelona are missing three defenders on the road. A Barcelona win by two or more is the unlikely outcome.

picks.label: Liverpool not to win by 3+
picks.reason: Liverpool are without Szoboszlai, Frimpong, Ekitike and Bradley (This Is Anfield), and Villarreal have scored two or three in both European games. A three-goal win looks unlikely.

picks.label: Betis not to win by 3+
picks.reason: Betis just gave up five at home to Barcelona and are missing striker Cucho Hernandez and Junior Firpo (Sports Mole), while Feyenoord have won five straight. Betis by three is a stretch.

picks.label: Fenerbahce not to win by 3+
picks.reason: Fenerbahce have been outscored badly in Europe this year and Asensio is doubtful, while Slavia lead their league on a four-game winning run. Previews expect a one-goal game.

picks.label: Bayern not to win by 2+
picks.reason: Bayern are without Olise, who is suspended, and Musiala, who is hurt (Bavarian Football Works), and the books have the game nearly even. A two-goal Bayern win is the unlikely part.

picks.label: AS Roma not to win by 3+
picks.reason: Roma are missing their starting goalkeeper Svilar plus Kone, Cristante and likely Dybala (Yahoo Sports, Sports Mole), and still haven't won in Europe this season. Winning by three with a patched-up side is a big ask.

picks.label: Man City not to win by 3+
picks.reason: Haaland has a knock and is expected to be rested, and Semenyo is out for two months (Sports Mole, beIN). City are in poor form and a three-goal margin without their striker is less likely than the price says.

picks.label: South Alabama to win
picks.reason: Marshall's coach won't name a quarterback before kickoff after calling his starter's play horrible (Herald-Dispatch), while South Alabama is unbeaten in conference with a confirmed starter and a strong run game. ESPN's model and the books both side with South Alabama.

picks.label: Under 224.5 points
picks.reason: Both teams were top defenses last year, and NBC Sports reports the point total has been bet down from 224.5 to about 220.5 since it opened. This bet still pays if the game stays under 224.5.

picks.label: Raptors to win + Barcelona not to win by 2+
picks.reason: Two of the outcomes I'm most sure about: a healthy Raptors team beats a Bulls team without its center, and a near-even PSG-Barcelona game doesn't end in a two-goal Barcelona win.
